Theme audit: decisions needed

Drawn with the prototype's real tokens (src/styles/tokens.css), not screenshots. The number under each sample is measured live in this page; the target is 4.5:1 for text and 3:1 for focus rings. Nothing on this page has been changed in the app yet.

1. Focus ring is too faint (both themes)

Where: Every button, tab, link and field (global focus ring, plus Button, Tabs, Chip, Checkbox, ThemeSwitch).

--line-ring is orange at 55% opacity. A focus indicator needs 3:1 against what is next to it. Proposal: draw the ring in --primary-primary-text (deep orange in Light, bright orange in Dark), same 2px gap + 2px ring. Ideally the line/ring token itself changes in the Figma theme.

2. White initials on blue and pink avatars (both themes)

Where: Avatar tones 2 and 4: the signed-in user (IFPI user, Dev), people on Rules and Country pages. Tones 1 and 3 already use dark initials.

White on --chart-chart-4 pink is 3.8:1 and on --chart-chart-2 blue 3.8:1 (needs 4.5:1). Proposal: dark initials (--primary-primary-foreground) on every tone, so all four match.

3. Green "up" text is slightly too light (Light only)

Where: Delta on stat tiles (Song, Artist, Country headers) and the Change column in a selected row.

--status-success-text in Light is green-600 #038251: 4.3:1 on a muted tile and 4.1:1 on a selected row. This is a token value (I have not edited tokens). Proposal: green-700 #096941 for Light status/success-text in Figma. Dark is fine.

4. Amber badge text is slightly too light (Light only)

Where: "Conflict" chip and the "In Progress" badge in the rights conflict card (Data split view).

--status-warning-text in Light is amber-700 #9e6802: 4.0 to 4.4:1 on the amber tints (the in-app card is the 4.0 end). Also a token value. Proposal: amber-800 #744c04 for Light status/warning-text.

5. Orange chip and current page number (Light only)

Where: Market chip on Data and entity pages; current page in Pagination.

Deep orange text on --surface-accent-strong is 4.4:1. Proposal: use the paler --surface-accent fill in these two components (5.1:1). In Dark nothing changes visibly: both fills read as orange tint.

6. Grey text in a selected table row (Light only)

Where: Date, ISRC, market and licensor columns of the selected row (Data, all tabs).

Muted grey on the orange 12% row is 4.4:1, just under 4.5:1. Two options: accept it (it is marginal and only on one row), or make secondary text in the selected row use the normal text colour.

7. Saved prompt tiles look disabled (Light only)

Where: Ask home, "Saved prompts" row.

The tiles use a glass gradient (secondary button fills) that reads as glass on dark but as flat grey on light, next to white cards elsewhere. Text contrast passes; this is a look-and-feel call. Proposal: white card fill (--surface-card) with the normal border in Light; Dark stays as designed.
